problem: try_submit and try_recv use single CAS without retry loop. If CAS fails (concurrent modification or spurious), operation returns false even when it should succeed. Lock-free algorithm representation is incorrect.
fix: Wrap CAS in loop: loop { match compare_exchange(...) { Ok(_) => return true, Err(_) => continue } }

problem: memory_ingress_multi_producer claims '3 producers x 3 consumers' but only spawns 1 thread via loom::thread::spawn. q2 and q3 are cloned but never spawned (dropped unused). Consumer runs on main thread sequentially.
fix: Spawn all 3 producers with loom::thread::spawn. Current code: only q1 is spawned; q2 and q3 go unused.

problem: check_invariant asserts q <= capacity twice. Second assertion has message 'underflow' which checks upper bound (wrong message). Also q >= 0 is guaranteed by usize in Rust.
fix: Remove duplicate assertion or fix message to 'queued {} exceeds capacity {}'

problem: All ipc_server_clients tests are serialized by single mutex. No concurrent interleavings explored — all operations are fully serialized. loom explores order of mutex acquisition but since each operation is atomic under mutex, no partial-operation interleavings exist.
fix: This is correct for mutex-based model but provides weak evidence for concurrency. Document that SharedClientMap serializes all operations. For stronger evidence, test would need fine-grained locking or separate atomic counters.

problem: write_buffer_concurrent spawns 2 threads but both serialize on same mutex. fill and drain are each single locked operations so no partial-operation interleavings.
fix: This is correct for mutex-based model but provides limited interleaving coverage. Consider testing WouldBlock path with concurrent fill.

problem: frame_pool_capacity_boundary pre-populates 4 frames then takes 1 (leaving 3), then releases. Does not test 'release when full causes silent drop' race condition — pool is at 3 when release happens, so frame is added not dropped.
fix: Fill to capacity, take 1 to bring below capacity, then test concurrent release at boundary. Or restructure: fill to capacity, spawn thread to take, then release races at full capacity.

problem: EXISTING-001..005 (existing loom models) are claimed to pass but no evidence of re-run is provided. Proof-writer report says 're-run to confirm stability' but provides no output.
fix: Re-run existing loom models with RUSTFLAGS='--cfg loom' cargo test -p vb_runtime <model> to confirm stability. Attach output to proof evidence.
